5.3 The duties of the Officers shall be:

(a) Chairperson – to preside at all meetings of the Club and of the Committee, and to represent the Club at official functions.

(b) Vice-Chairperson – to assist the Chairperson and to preside in the Chairperson’s absence.

(c) Secretary – to conduct the correspondence of the Club, to keep the minutes of all meetings, to give due notice of meetings, and to maintain the Club’s records.

(d) Treasurer – to receive and bank all monies, to keep proper accounts, to prepare a statement of accounts for the Annual General Meeting, and to make payments as authorised by the Committee.

(e) Membership Secretary – to maintain the register of members, to collect subscriptions, and to issue membership cards.

(f) Child Welfare Officer – to act as the first point of contact for any safeguarding concern, to ensure that the Club’s safeguarding policy is implemented, and to liaise with the relevant authorities as required.

(g) Other officers – to perform such duties as the Committee shall assign.

5.4 In the event of a vacancy, the Committee may co-opt a Full or Life Member to fill the office until the next Annual General Meeting.

---

ARTICLE 6 – THE COMMITTEE

6.1 The affairs of the Club shall be managed by a Committee consisting of the Officers and not fewer than four nor more than eight other Full or Life Members, all elected at the Annual General Meeting.

6.2 The Committee shall meet at least once every two months. The quorum shall be five members of the Committee.

6.3 The Committee shall have power to:

(a) appoint sub-committees for specific purposes;

(b) enter into contracts on behalf of the Club;

(c) borrow money on behalf of the Club, up to a limit of £5,000, subject to the approval of a General Meeting for any larger sum;
ARTICLE 6 – THE COMMITTEE (continued)

6.4 The Committee may, at its discretion, invite any member to attend a meeting of the Committee in an advisory capacity. Such a member shall not be entitled to vote.

6.5 The Committee shall keep a record of all decisions taken at its meetings, and such records shall be available for inspection by any Full or Life Member at a reasonable time upon request to the Secretary.

6.6 The Committee shall report on its activities at each Annual General Meeting.

6.7 Any member of the Committee who is absent from three consecutive meetings without apology accepted by the Committee may be deemed to have resigned, and the vacancy shall be filled in accordance with Clause 5.4.

---

ARTICLE 7 – GENERAL MEETINGS

7.1 The Annual General Meeting of the Club shall be held in each calendar year, not later than the end of March, at a time and place determined by the Committee.

7.2 The business of the Annual General Meeting shall include:
(a) the consideration of the report of the Committee;
(b) the consideration of the statement of accounts;
(c) the election of Officers and other Committee members;
(d) the appointment of an independent examiner, where required;
(e) the transaction of any other business of which due notice has been given.

7.3 An Extraordinary General Meeting may be called at any time by the Committee, and shall be called by the Secretary upon the written request of not fewer than ten Full or Life Members, stating the business to be considered.

7.4 At least fourteen clear days’ notice of any General Meeting shall be given to all members, stating the business to be considered. No business other than that stated in the notice shall be transacted at an Extraordinary General Meeting.

7.5 The quorum for a General Meeting shall be fifteen members, or one-tenth of the Full and Life Members, whichever is the lesser, present in person or by proxy. If a quorum is not present within thirty minutes of the time appointed, the meeting shall stand adjourned to a date, time and place determined by the Committee, and notice of the adjourned meeting shall be given to all members.

7.6 At General Meetings, the Chairperson shall preside, or in their absence the Vice-Chairperson, or in the absence of both, a Chairperson shall be elected by the members present.

7.7 Each Full Member and Life Member shall have one vote. Voting shall normally be by a show of hands, but a secret ballot shall be taken if requested by not fewer than five members present. In the case of an equality of votes, the Chairperson of the meeting shall have a second or casting vote.

7.8 The Chairperson’s ruling on any point of order shall be final, subject to the provisions of Clause 12.4.

---

ARTICLE 8 – FINANCE

8.1 The financial year of the Club shall end on the 31st day of December in each year.

8.2 The Treasurer shall keep proper accounting records and shall present a statement of accounts to the Annual General Meeting. The accounts shall be examined by an independent examiner appointed at the Annual General Meeting, unless the Committee resolves that an audit is required.

8.3 The bank account of the Club shall be held in the name of the Club, and withdrawals shall require the signatures of two authorised signatories, of whom one shall be the Treasurer. The Committee shall approve the list of authorised signatories.

8.4 All monies received on behalf of the Club shall be paid into the Club’s bank account within seven days of receipt, save where the Committee resolves otherwise for a particular purpose.

8.5 The Committee shall have power to authorise expenditure on behalf of the Club up to a limit of £2,000 for any single item. Any expenditure exceeding this limit shall require the approval of a General Meeting.

ARTICLE 6 – THE COMMITTEE (continued)

6.4 The Committee may, at its discretion, invite any member to attend a meeting of the Committee in an advisory capacity. Such a member shall not be entitled to vote.

6.5 The Committee shall keep a record of all decisions taken at its meetings, and such records shall be available for inspection by any Full or Life Member at a reasonable time upon request to the Secretary.

6.6 The Committee shall report on its activities at each Annual General Meeting.

6.7 Any member of the Committee who is absent from three consecutive meetings without apology accepted by the Committee may be deemed to have resigned, and the vacancy shall be filled in accordance with Clause 5.4.

---

ARTICLE 7 – GENERAL MEETINGS

7.1 The Annual General Meeting of the Club shall be held in each calendar year, not later than the end of March, at a time and place determined by the Committee.

7.2 The business of the Annual General Meeting shall include:
(a) the consideration of the report of the Committee;
(b) the consideration of the statement of accounts;
(c) the election of Officers and other Committee members;
(d) the appointment of an independent examiner, where required;
(e) the transaction of any other business of which due notice has been given.

7.3 An Extraordinary General Meeting may be called at any time by the Committee, and shall be called by the Secretary upon the written request of not fewer than ten Full or Life Members, stating the business to be considered.

7.4 At least fourteen clear days’ notice of any General Meeting shall be given to all members, stating the business to be considered. No business other than that stated in the notice shall be transacted at an Extraordinary General Meeting.

7.5 The quorum for a General Meeting shall be fifteen members, or one-tenth of the Full and Life Members, whichever is the lesser, present in person or by proxy. If a quorum is not present within thirty minutes of the time appointed, the meeting shall stand adjourned to a date, time and place determined by the Committee, and notice of the adjourned meeting shall be given to all members.

7.6 At General Meetings, the Chairperson shall preside, or in their absence the Vice-Chairperson, or in the absence of both, a Chairperson shall be elected by the members present.

7.7 Each Full Member and Life Member shall have one vote. Voting shall normally be by a show of hands, but a secret ballot shall be taken if requested by not fewer than five members present. In the case of an equality of votes, the Chairperson of the meeting shall have a second or casting vote.

7.8 The Chairperson’s ruling on any point of order shall be final, subject to the provisions of Clause 12.4.

---

ARTICLE 8 – FINANCE

8.1 The financial year of the Club shall end on the 31st day of December in each year.

8.2 The Treasurer shall keep proper accounting records and shall present a statement of accounts to the Annual General Meeting. The accounts shall be examined by an independent examiner appointed at the Annual General Meeting, unless the Committee resolves that an audit is required.

8.3 The bank account of the Club shall be held in the name of the Club, and withdrawals shall require the signatures of two authorised signatories, of whom one shall be the Treasurer. The Committee shall approve the list of authorised signatories.

8.4 All monies received on behalf of the Club shall be paid into the Club’s bank account within seven days of receipt, save where the Committee resolves otherwise for a particular purpose.

8.5 The Committee shall have power to authorise expenditure on behalf of the Club up to a limit of £2,000 for any single item. Any expenditure exceeding this limit shall require the approval of a General Meeting.

D1. The maximum occupancy of the main hall shall not exceed 250 persons at any one time. This figure includes staff, performers, and officials. The Club shall display a notice stating the maximum occupancy adjacent to the main entrance.

D2. Use of the premises is restricted to the purposes of a sports and social club, including matches, training, social events, committee meetings, and lettings to affiliated community groups. Any other use, or any use likely to increase the fire risk, requires prior written approval from the Council.

D3. The premises shall not be used for sleeping accommodation.

D4. All fire doors shall be maintained in working order and shall not be wedged open. Self-closing devices must be checked monthly by the Club's designated Fire Warden.

D5. Flammable liquids and gases shall not be stored within the building except for small quantities of cleaning materials and lighter fuel, kept in the locked metal cabinet in the lobby.

D6. The Club shall ensure that a competent person carries out a fire risk assessment at least annually, and that the findings are recorded and made available to the Council on request.

D7. Any alterations to the building, its services, or its layout that could affect fire safety must be notified to the Council before work commences.

---

**SECTION E — RECOMMENDATIONS**

The following items are not conditions of this certificate but are strongly recommended to improve safety and accessibility:

- **Rear exit path:** The grassed area immediately outside the rear exit is uneven. The Club should level this path and consider installing a temporary ramp to improve access for wheelchair users and those with limited mobility. This was also noted at the previous inspection.

- **Kitchen extractor fan:** The extractor fan over the cooker is operational but noisy. The Club should arrange for it to be serviced and, if necessary, replaced. A build-up of grease was observed on the filter.

- **Assembly point signage:** The route from the rear exit to the assembly point (car park) is not clearly signed. Consider adding a weatherproof sign showing the direction to the assembly point.

- **First aid kit:** The contents of the first aid kit in the kitchen were checked and found to be complete, but the kit itself is small. For events with more than 100 people, consider providing a second, larger kit.

- **Electrical socket covers:** Two socket covers in the main hall were loose. These should be replaced to prevent accidental damage and to comply with good practice.

1. Welcome and Apologies
The Chair, James Whitfield, welcomed members and noted that apologies had been received from those listed above. He confirmed that a quorum was present (22 members in attendance, exceeding the constitutionally required minimum of 15).

2. Minutes of the Previous AGM (16 March 2023)
The minutes of the 2023 AGM had been circulated with the agenda. There were no matters arising not already covered elsewhere on tonight's agenda. Proposed by P. Doyle, seconded by A. Bell, that the minutes be approved as a true record. Motion carried.

3. Chair's Report
J. Whitfield presented the annual report for the year ending 31 December 2023. He highlighted the following:

- Senior men's XI finished 3rd in Division Two of the Westshire League, their highest placing since 2019.
- The women's XI, re-formed in 2022, completed their first full season in the County Women's League, finishing 6th of 8.
- Youth section continued to grow, with U13 and U15 boys' teams plus a new U14 girls' team starting in September.
- The club's application to the Sport England Community Asset Fund was unsuccessful in October, but the committee had since revised the clubhouse refurbishment plans and intended to reapply later this year.
- The annual summer barbecue and the winter quiz night together raised £1,340 for the junior kit fund.

He thanked the outgoing committee, the grounds staff, and the many volunteers who had helped with pitch maintenance and match-day catering. He noted that the club had received a small grant from Thornwick Parish Council (£500) towards new training equipment, which had been purchased in December.

4. Treasurer's Report and Accounts
P. Doyle presented the accounts for the year ended 31 December 2023, copies of which had been circulated. Key points:

- Income for the year was £48,210, up from £42,880 in 2022.
- Expenditure was £44,670, leaving a surplus of £3,540.
- The club's reserves stood at £12,760 at year end.
- The increase in income was largely due to higher bar takings and increased membership fees following the rise in adult subs from £60 to £70 per year, approved at the 2023 AGM.

P. Doyle explained that the clubhouse roof repair, originally estimated at £4,500, had come in at £5,200 due to additional timber work. This had been met from the general reserve. He proposed that the accounts be adopted. Seconded by R. Singh. Motion carried.

documents.content:
**Thornwick Community Sports Club – Committee Meeting Minutes**
**Held Monday 8 April 2024, 7.30pm, Clubhouse Bar**
**Present:** J. Okafor (Chair), M. Chen (Treasurer), T. Barnes (Fixture Secretary), K. Marr (Social Secretary), P. Singh (Welfare Officer), L. Doyle (Junior Section Lead), A. Whitfield (Clubhouse Manager), R. Hale (Grounds)
**Apologies:** S. Patel (Secretary – on holiday), D. Ives (Press Officer)
**Minutes of last meeting:** Approved – motion carried, proposed P. Singh, seconded K. Marr.

---

**1. Matters Arising**

1.1 The Chair confirmed that the Parish Council had not yet responded on the parking issue. He had left a further message with the clerk’s office on 2 April. The matter remained open. **Action: J. Okafor** to chase again by Friday 12 April.

1.2 The pitch maintenance works had been booked with the grounds contractor for the week commencing 10 June. R. Hale confirmed that the overseeding and rolling would be completed before the first home friendly on 27 July. The cost estimate of £1,200 remained unchanged.

1.3 The kit order for the junior section was placed on 20 March with the club’s usual supplier. Delivery was expected in early May. L. Doyle asked whether the order included the new away socks; the Treasurer confirmed that the £500 figure covered socks, shorts and two sets of shirts as agreed at the AGM.

---

**2. Junior Fixtures and Survey Update**

2.1 L. Doyle reported that the junior section had received its league fixtures. There were 14 home matches across the U11 and U13 teams. The first home fixture was scheduled for Saturday 21 September.

2.2 The survey on the proposed opening of the clubhouse during junior matches had received 47 responses so far, with a closing date of Friday 12 April. Initial feedback was broadly positive, though a number of respondents raised concerns about safeguarding and the need for a designated supervisor. P. Singh noted that a rota would need to be drawn up if the proposal went ahead. The full report would be presented at the next committee meeting as previously agreed.

---

**3. Treasurer’s Report**

3.1 M. Chen presented the updated cash flow forecast. The forecast showed a small surplus of £240 for the year, following the receipt of a £300 donation from the Thornwick Traders’ Association. The donation was made in March and was not included in the earlier forecast.

3.2 The bar stock order of £1,500 had been placed on 2 April. A. Whitfield confirmed that the delivery would arrive on Thursday 11 April and that the cellar had been cleaned and prepared.

3.3 The Treasurer reminded the committee that the County League affiliation fee had increased by 5% for the coming season. This had been budgeted for and the final invoice of £1,890 was due by 30 April. The Treasurer would process the payment.

3.4 The committee discussed the cost of the clubhouse roof repair. The final invoice of £5,200 had been paid in February. No further roof work was anticipated this year.

---

**4. Fixture Secretary’s Report**

4.1 T. Barnes circulated the confirmed fixture list for the coming season. The club would have 18 home matches, with the first game at home on Saturday 14 September. The pre-season friendlies were still to be arranged. He would circulate the finalised list to members once the friendlies were confirmed.

4.2 T. Barnes reported that the County League had introduced a new rule regarding the use of substitutes. Each team could now name up to five substitutes, with a maximum of three used during a match. The committee noted the change.

4.3 The groundsman had advised that the main pitch would need to be marked out for the junior matches as well as the senior matches. R. Hale confirmed that the marking machine was in working order and that paint had been ordered.
